Boundaries.Import: Whole script locally, or submit + 50ms completion polling + pipeline retrieval; fixture decoding and batch JSON preparation included

Metadata.Connection: tcp:127.0.0.1,1433; TLS encrypted, server certificate trusted without validation; explicit pooling modes; authentication recorded separately
Metadata.IndexComparison: Counterbalanced paired reuse reads; ten checked warm-ups after each condition change

Protocol.IndexComparison: Counterbalanced paired reuse reads; ten checked warm-ups after each condition change

Evidence.Preservation: Checksum COPY_ONLY native backups of all three measured databases; operational backup actually restored and field-checked; source/schema metadata retained independently of installed server

Integrity.Command: DBCC CHECKDB WITH NO_INFOMSGS, ALL_ERRORMSGS, TABLERESULTS

Limitations: Separate warm local provider passes on the same host/storage; neither paired trials nor isolated engine speed.
At most 10,000 synthetic records, repeated ASCII x payloads. SQL Server uses uncompressed Unicode JSON text and rows; PostgreSQL uses JSONB with unusually effective TOAST compression.

SQL Server uses JSON text, typed nonpersisted computed columns and B-tree indexes; native SQL Server 2025 JSON type/JSON indexes were not measured. Corrected passes counterbalance paired index-present/absent reuse reads and warm each condition ten times; historical passes used a separate scan phase.
SQL Server document projection returns typed columns rather than constructing another JSON object in SQL; object mapping and complete fields remain inside the client boundary.
Direct outer Measure-Command clocks include helper return and connection disposal; serialization/checks follow clocks. SQLite used Stopwatch. No subtraction of harness overhead.

Memory/cache budgets and encryption differ. SQL Server defaults permit dynamic memory growth and use encrypted TCP trusting the local certificate; PostgreSQL used SSL disabled. Fresh connections include the selected authentication and TLS setup.
SQL Server/PG endpoints use pooled connections; SQLite endpoints did not. SQL Server direct new/reuse/pooled modes expose the connection choice.

Per-row writes send one prepared statement per row; OPENJSON set variants send one JSON request and commit once. Batch JSON is outside database timers and inside whole-import clocks. Work tables lack the main filter index.

Authentication and identities are recorded separately for discovery and workloads. SQL login mode uses a non-sysadmin owner of dedicated databases; Windows baseline used sysadmin. Neither is a production least-privilege service identity. No remote host, frontend, sustained capacity, cold cache, crash, PITR or HA testing.
No SQL Server endpoint concurrency. Default read committed used locks with RCSI disabled; repeatable read held shared locks. Snapshot isolation was disabled and not tested.

One-second host samples cannot attribute individual requests; sqlservr CPU values were unavailable under this diagnostic identity, so its CPU delta is null. Agent/tool activity was not isolated or given a paired SQL Server control.
Seven sequential observations per case and three measured concurrency bursts support bounded choices, not capacity or precise tail estimates.
